name: Etching
region: Southern Germany, then Lorraine, Amsterdam and Venice
summary: The artist draws with a needle through a wax ground on a metal plate, and acid bites the lines. The line is free like a pen line. Callot made it exact; Rembrandt made it dark and alive, with tone from hatching and from ink left on the plate.

philosophy.core_thesis: A needle that moves through wax as easily as a pen gives the artist a free line, and the acid gives it depth.
design_principles: Draw with a free, even line of the needle; the width comes from the time in the acid, not from the pressure of the hand.
Make the dark parts by more layers of hatching and by a longer bite: stop out the light lines and bite the dark ones again.
Use hatching in 1–4 directions; let the lines be loose and a little irregular.
Leave a film of ink on the plate (plate tone) for a soft dark where the image needs atmosphere.
Keep a wide margin and a clear plate mark.
Print in a warm black or a brown-black on a cream or a Japanese paper.
anti_patterns: Mechanical hatching with an equal pitch everywhere
Lines that swell like a burin line
Flat colour or a halftone screen
A hard, black edge round every form

process.matrix: A copper or iron plate, coated with an acid-resistant ground of wax, resin and asphalt.
process.press: A roller press with felt blankets, as for engraving.
process.image_making: The artist draws through the ground with a needle, bites the plate in acid in stages, cleans it, and proofs it.
process.edition: Some tens to some hundreds; the artist often prints each impression with a different wipe.

inks.strategy: One warm black or brown-black ink; the artist wipes it with tarlatan and the hand and leaves some on the plate.

screening.rule: Make the tone with 1–4 layers of free hatching at 50–100 a inch and with plate tone.

registration.rule: One plate prints all the image; there is no register.

substrate.stock: Laid rag paper, or Japanese gampi and kozo paper for a warm, soft impression.
substrate.finish: Soft, dampened before the print; Japanese papers are smooth and thin.

surface.impression: A plate mark and lines that stand up a little from the paper.
surface.sheen: Matt to a soft gloss; plate tone is matt.
surface.texture: A living web of thin lines, with a haze of plate tone in the darks.

positive: quiet landscape and scenes of daily life
warm black ink on cream paper

emotion.target_response: Intimacy and atmosphere: the viewer sees the hand of the artist, and the darks feel deep and quiet.

avoid_when: The picture must read at a small size on a screen.
The brand needs bright, flat colour.

modifiers.how: Cut swelling burin lines in systems, with an equal pitch and no plate tone.
Rock the full plate black and scrape the lights; drop the line.
